newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to impose import tariffs on U.S corn syrup.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to impose import tariffs on U.S corn syrup.

text.p: Mexico's Trade Ministry said Tuesday it had decided to impose provisional import tariffs on imports from the United States of high fructose corn syrup (HFCS).

The move, which will be announced officially in the government's Official Gazette on Wednesday, comes after Mexico's sugar industry requested the Trade Ministry investigate corn syrup import dumping allegations.
Tariffs of between $66.50 and $125.30 per tonne will be imposed on grade 42 HFCS and between $63.40 and $175.50 per tonne of grade 55 HFCS, it added.
"These tariffs are equivalent to an average dumping margin of 102.2 percent for grade 42 syrup and 61.1 percent for grade 55 fructose," the ministry said in a statement.
It did not say when the provisional tariffs would be applied to the alternative sweetner, although edicts in the Official Gazette are normally applicable from the date of publication.

The ministry added it would still continue its investigation into the dumping allegations against U.S. exporters and Mexican-based importers in order to arrive at a final resolution. It gave no timeframe.

Mexico's National Sugar Chamber, the umbrella group for the country's mill owners, launched its campaign to have tariffs imposed on HFCS imports on Feb 27, claiming imports at prices lower than production costs were damaging the national sugar industry.
